title: Dust substructures and line perturbations driven by a forming planet in J16120
question: What are the dust substructures and gas kinematic signatures of ongoing planet formation in the protoplanetary disc around 2MASS J16120668–301027?

data.angular_resolution: Continuum: 125 x 95 mas; 12CO: 181 x 145 mas; 13CO: 183 x 143 mas
data.sensitivity: Continuum: 0.021 mJy/beam; 12CO: 4.9 mJy/beam per 25 m/s channel; 13CO: 4.0 mJy/beam per 50 m/s channel

what.value: Self-calibrated Band 6 dust continuum observations of J16120

evidence.quote: Additionally, we use the self-calibrated Band 6 observations of J16120 presented in Li et al. (2025), in which data from programs 2021.1.00128.L (PI: Ke Zhang, Zhang et al. 2025) and 2022.1.00646.S (PI: Feng Long) were concatenated

what.value: 12CO (J=2-1) emission surface profile and Band 6 dust continuum image and background source flux

evidence.quote: Left panel of Figure 8 shows the vertical emission profile for the 12 CO (J=3–2) in this work, and 12 CO (J=2–1) in Sierra et al. (2024a).
This source was also observed in Band 6 in Sierra et al. (2024a), with a dust continuum flux of 0 . 12 ± 0 . 02 mJy.

what.value: Gas mass and CO depletion factor (Carbon depletion of 10) for J16120

evidence.quote: By modelling and comparing the obtained gas mass with the observed CO lines, Trapman et al. (2025) determined that the relative abundance of CO with respect to H 2 for J16120 is log 10 𝑥 CO = −4 . 82 + − 0 0 . . 11 18 , giving a CO depletion factor of ∼ 10

what.value: Positions of H-alpha and SPHERE K-band point source candidates

external_data.citation: Li et al. (2025); Ginski et al. (2025)

recipe.goal: Align executions, rescale fluxes, self-calibrate, and image continuum and CO lines
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian to low-resolution continuum per execution to align to common phase centre; scale fluxes to concatenated LB executions with gencal; phase self-calibrate SB (2 rounds) then SB+LB (1 round); apply tables to line data, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, regrid with cvel2, and image with multi-scale tclean down to 1 sigma
key_parameters: Self-cal solint: 'inf', '360s' for SB; 'inf' for combined SB+LB
Robust = 0.5 (continuum), 1.5 (12CO at 25 m/s), 2.0 (13CO at 50 m/s); clean threshold = 1 sigma

recipe.goal: Compute molecular moment maps, integrated fluxes, and disc radii (R68, R90)
recipe.method: Generate moment 0, peak intensity, and Gaussian velocity maps using Discminer with sigma clipping; measure R68, R90, and integrated fluxes using curve of growth (COG) within 4 arcsec
key_parameters: Clipping: 1 sigma for Moment 0; 3 sigma for peak intensity and peak velocity; outer radius cutoff = 4 arcsec

recipe.goal: Model axisymmetric dust continuum visibilities and radial spectral index
recipe.method: Extract continuum visibilities using export_uvtable normalising uv-distances per spw/channel; constrain inclination and PA by minimizing spread of real visibilities and centre by minimizing imaginary visibilities; fit non-parametric radial brightness profiles in Band 6 and Band 7 with Frankenstein; compute full Planck brightness temperature and spectral index profile
key_parameters: Geometry fixed to Band 6 values: inc = 37.0 deg, PA = 45.1 deg; Frankenstein hyperparameters: alpha = 1.05, w_smooth = 0.1
assumptions: Axisymmetric dust disc; full Planck function (without Rayleigh-Jeans approximation)

recipe.goal: Fit eccentric parametric dust disc model in the visibility plane
recipe.method: Model dust continuum with three eccentric Gaussian rings (g0, g23, g75); compute model visibilities with Galario and sample 13-parameter posterior with emcee
key_parameters: Pixel size = 10 mas, image size = 1024 pixels; fixed inc = 37.0 deg, PA = 45.1 deg; 13 free parameters; 104 walkers (8 x 13), 8000 steps
assumptions: Constant eccentricity e and periastron omega across the three Gaussian rings

recipe.goal: Model 12CO and 13CO channel maps and extract kinematic, line-width, and peak-intensity residuals
recipe.method: Fit 3D Keplerian channel map models to 12CO and 13CO cubes using discminer with emcee; fit Gaussian line profiles to data and best-fit model cubes to extract centroid velocity, line width, peak intensity, residual maps, and 3D velocity components (v_r, v_phi, v_z); test warped disc model on velocity residuals
key_parameters: 230 walkers; burn-in of 80,000 steps (12CO) and 30,000 steps (13CO) plus 10% sampling steps; 13CO inclination and PA fixed to 37.0 deg and 45.1 deg
assumptions: Keplerian rotation with differential rotation as a function of height z(r); exponentially tapered power-law surfaces for front and back sides

recipe.goal: Extract non-parametric CO emission surface, isothermal scale height, and estimate total disc gas mass
recipe.method: Extract 12CO (J=3-2) vertical emission surface with disksurf and fit with tapered power law; compute average elevation z/r within r < 120 au; compute isothermal scale height H_g from front-surface brightness temperature; infer gas mass from z/r and CO depletion factor using Paneque-Carreno et al. (2025) relations
key_parameters: SNR > 3 mask, fixed disc geometry (inc = 37.0 deg, PA = 45.1 deg) and offset, radial binning = 1/4 beam size; mean molecular weight mu = 2.3; M_star = 0.7 M_sun (for H_g) and 0.6 M_sun (for gas mass relation); Carbon depletion = 10
assumptions: 12CO (J=3-2) emission is optically thick so brightness temperature equals gas temperature; Carbon depletion factor = 10

score_reason: The paper provides a remarkably thorough quantitative recipe, including CASA version, self-calibration solution intervals, robust and velocity resolution grids, Frankenstein hyperparameters, Galario/emcee priors and walker setups, and full best-fit parameter tables in Appendix B. Minor deductions are for the missing Zenodo DOI, unstated tclean pixel/mask settings, and unstated per-execution flux/astrometric corrections.
rediscovery_reason: Raw ALMA data (2023.1.01100.S, 2021.1.00128.L, 2022.1.00646.S) and all primary analysis codes (CASA, Frankenstein, Galario, Discminer, disksurf, emcee) are public, and the main results (ring locations, disc eccentricity, dynamical stellar mass, line-width residual amplitude, and CO surface parameters) are precisely quantified.
